title: 4D-STEM Investigation of Point Defects in Off-Stoichiometric SrTiO3 for Memristive Switching Applications
content: Ferroelectric materials-based devices, like resistive random-access memory devices, have attracted significant attention due to their low power consumption, fast switching, and high durability. Among various materials, off-stoichiometric SrTiO3 grown by metal-organic vapor phase epitaxy (MOVPE) has shown exceptional on/off ratios exceeding 1000, making it a promising ReRAM candidate [1]. However, a deeper understanding of the specific defects responsible for these enhanced switching properties remains crucial.
